statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. NVIDIA-led risk sentiment remains constructive, but current evidence does not verify persistent one-way NQ structure.
recommendation: Tail remains below the WATCH band; the next concentrated checkpoint is the 12:30 UTC U.S. data cluster and subsequent cash-open price discovery.
headline: NVIDIA support persists while one-way NQ structure remains unverified
body: Reuters reported NVIDIA up 4.7% after hours, S&P 500 e-mini futures up 0.3%, the U.S. 10-year yield down 1 basis point at 4.652%, and Brent lower. The cross-asset mix is constructive but insufficient to establish a pathological no-retracement Nasdaq-100 path.

lookbackSummary: Across the prior 24 clock-hours, Tail was low before Wednesday's U.S. data and NVIDIA earnings, moved into WATCH during the delayed earnings-call reversal, peaked at 24% overnight, then eased below WATCH as broader confirmation moderated. No assessment is available for 06:00 UTC.
outlookSummary: Residual NVIDIA strength supports technology sentiment, but lower oil and a slightly lower 10-year yield limit cross-asset confirmation. The next concentrated risk window is the 12:30 UTC U.S. data cluster through the cash-open follow-through period.

forecast.analysis: Current evidence is constructive but incomplete: Reuters reported NVIDIA up 4.7% after hours, S&P 500 e-mini futures up 0.3%, the U.S. 10-year yield at 4.652% and Brent lower. No fresh persistent one-way NQ price path is independently verified.

forecast.analysis: European cash-open liquidity is a conditional normalization test. Tail remains low unless technology strength broadens into sustained index-level extension with shallow or failed retracements.
Early European trade should clarify whether the NVIDIA impulse is broadening or fading. Ordinary retracements would support a normal regime; repeated extension would raise conditional Tail.
Later European trade bridges into the U.S. premarket. A renewed semiconductor-led bid could increase directional risk, while lower oil and stable yields would limit cross-asset confirmation.
As U.S. participation builds, event proximity raises Stress. Tail stays below WATCH unless price action begins to show sustained directional efficiency rather than ordinary pre-data positioning.
The 12:30 UTC U.S. claims and advance trade/inventory releases create a concentrated repricing window. WATCH reflects conditional event-path risk, not an assumption that one-way structure will occur.
Post-data price discovery and the approach to the cash open create the day's highest conditional Tail window. Fast retracing moves would remain whipsaw stress; failed pullbacks would raise path risk.
The U.S. cash open is the key directional-efficiency checkpoint. WATCH persists conditionally; only sustained extension with weak retracements would justify moving beyond the watch band.
The first full cash-session hour should reveal whether opening moves persist or mean-revert. Tail can ease quickly if breadth and price action normalize after the opening auction.
Mid-morning U.S. trade remains a secondary follow-through test. Without repeated extension or session-extreme holding, the base case shifts back toward mixed conditions.
Late morning should carry less event intensity if the data/opening impulse has stabilized. Renewed one-way technology extension would be the main condition for Tail to re-enter WATCH.
The U.S. midday period is expected to be lower intensity unless a delayed second leg develops. Stable yields, oil and ordinary pullbacks would keep Tail low.
Early afternoon remains a normalization window. Conditional risk would rise only if the session develops persistent directional efficiency after earlier retracements fail.
With no scheduled top-tier catalyst in this hour, path structure dominates. Two-way trade keeps Tail low; repeated extension toward session extremes would challenge the normal regime.
As afternoon liquidity develops, renewed semiconductor or megacap alignment could increase directional conviction. Absent that alignment, mixed trade remains the base case.
The approach to the final cash-session hours raises continuation risk modestly. WATCH is conditional on a coherent late-day trend rather than on clock time alone.
Late-session positioning can amplify an established move. Tail remains WATCH only if breadth and price action align with persistent extension; otherwise stress should decay.
Into the closing hour, conditional continuation risk remains modestly elevated. A balanced close or meaningful retracement would favor normalization over a pathological one-way path.
After the U.S. close, the main test is whether any late-session impulse persists into thinner liquidity. Without fresh extension, Tail should return to low.
Early after-hours trade is expected to be lower intensity absent a new verified catalyst. The risk focus shifts from event stress to whether the day's direction persists without retracement.
As after-hours liquidity thins, the base case is normalization. A new geopolitical or technology headline could lift Stress, but Tail requires corresponding one-way price-path evidence.
The overnight transition should remain low Tail if cross-assets stay orderly. A sharp futures gap with aligned technology and yields would be the principal conditional invalidation.
Early Asian-session liquidity may reprice the prior U.S. move. Tail stays low unless renewed technology leadership produces repeated extension with shallow pullbacks.

By the next European pre-open, attention begins shifting toward Friday's Jackson Hole keynote later in the day. Event anticipation may raise Stress, but not Tail without observed directional structure.
